results.evidence: I ran the exact AC invocation through cottonwood.cli.main with utc_now pinned to 2026-12-01T00:00:00Z against a freshly migrated temp db. It returned rc 0 and printed 'run 1 recorded: research-prospects 1.0.0, 3.25 USD (claude-code-cost)'. The single agent_runs row was (1, research-prospects, 1.0.0, claude-opus-5-5, 2026-11-30T16:00:00Z, 2026-11-30T16:40:00Z, 'brief: GC firms in Salt Lake County', out/research/2026-11-30-gc.json, passed, 120000, '3.25', claude-code-cost, 0). Every field matches the AC. The test test_run_is_stored_with_every_field also passes.

I ran tests/test_record_run.py and all 24 tests passed. Three of them cover this AC through the real CLI entry point `main`. test_estimated_cost_is_marked checks that --estimated gives cost_estimated 1 and a line ending '(claude-code-cost, estimated)'. test_billing_console_source_is_stored checks that billing-console is accepted and stored. test_recorded_runs_feed_the_report records a 3.25 observed run and a 1.1 estimated run, then runs `report --from 2026-11-30 --to 2026-11-30`. It asserts the exact lines '- Model cost: 4.35', '- Model cost observed: 3.25' and '- Model cost estimated: 1.10'. The implementation matches: cottonwood/cli.py has an --estimated store_true flag and COST_SOURCES includes billing-console. RunRecord.line appends ', estimated' when the flag is set, and record_run stores int(cost_estimated). cottonwood/report.py sums observed and estimated costs separately in _model_cost, with the labels at lines 58-60. I tried a manual end-to-end probe with a scratch database, but the sandbox policy blocked it. The verdict therefore rests on the passing tests plus reading the code.
